## Scope, authority and independence

The assessed M2 implementation is 75f13e09 against M1 handoff a582dbe1. Approved Skill/System and plan remain unchanged; design-review-r2 and delivery-review-r2 supply governing package decisions. Prior Design subject readings are reused only for unchanged authority or byte-identical archived source content. Original source and pilot hashes in upstream reviews describe their inspected baseline, not approval of every subsequent implementation. Current M2 subjects bind realized transfer separately. The independent reviewer authored none of the implementation, source dispositions, tests or evidence notes; earlier Design and M1 reviews were assessments only. No engineering, activity or work state was edited.

Read evidence includes m2-implementation.md, the actual full source/consumer diff, complete retained Skill Contract, the approved precise retained-contract table and displacement maps, archive navigation and original identities, validator/test changes, and the parent-provided full-branch CI failure. Record Format RF-SR-01/02/03 and its exact record definition were inspected because this new integration failure requires distinguishing authoritative stage narrative from engineering subjects.

## Substantive source and integration assessment

The common contract is transferred to the approved precise Skill owner. Metadata fields and selected profile, role fields/two-line summary/stage vocabulary, single authoritative vocabulary presentation and approved reference placement, complete output equivalents, portability surfaces/exclusions, bounded legacy prefixes/fail-or-explicit-exception, new/changed versus inventory enforcement, evidence-reading escapes and claim boundaries have actionable current destinations. The implementation does not weaken the corrected table or silently broaden pilot-only SKL-SR-16–19.

The mixed Skill Contract keeps R37–45 and R56–63 with source IDs, specialist-owner boundaries, superseded runtime-proof clauses and completed rollout restrictions/budgets explicitly distinguished. Contract-era examples retain context and do not reactivate retired names/storage. Mixed architecture replaces exactly the common building-block portion, resource flow 1–7, four crosscutting paragraphs and resource ADR navigation; Gate B/materialization/no-agent-runtime items 8–10 and other responsibilities remain. Governance and necessary current navigation point to Skill under reviewed implementation plus successful Verify, not an early adoption claim.

Independent raw-byte comparison against a582dbe1 proves all four archive snapshots equal their pre-M2 originals. The three fully superseded source-path copies remain byte-identical for source-relative historical links. All 73 archive-navigation local targets resolve. The pre-existing illustrative missing plan target is expressly documented; preserved snapshot-relative links are supplemented with source-resolved navigation as the approved Design allows. No operational resources, schema, manifests, methods, historical judgments or complete directory were moved. M1 skill/package subjects remain unchanged.

The three literal historical source tests now explicitly assess archived history; current-owner tests separately protect preserved presentation/enforcement details and identities. No test was deleted or weakened merely to pass. Guide-system protection now includes the actual new owner and a negative stale-guide-authority mutation. The new selector allowance is a closed five-path archive set selecting skills.regression, with unknown archive paths still blocked; it does not grant arbitrary archive exemptions. This compatibility correction is consistent with the approved necessary consumer scope.

One cross-milestone integration defect prevents approval: full-branch CI rejects the nine new stage-owned Markdown narrative sidecars. Local M2 CI only covered its selected working scope and did not establish full-branch viability. The narrative content is useful and was relied upon, but must be represented consistently with the current JSON recording contract rather than opening a second stage record surface or weakening selector protection. See skl-cr-001.

## First-pass checklist

| Item | Result | Evidence and rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Spec alignment | concern | Source transfer implements the approved map precisely; stage-owned narrative sidecars conflict with RF-SR-01 storage and prevent integrated validation. |
| 2. Test coverage | pass within implemented scope | 358 skill tests, nine guide tests and focused archive-selector red/green cover changed ownership/navigation and failure routing. Historical assertions retain identity intent; current ones guard actual surviving fields/populations. Correction requires fresh direct proof. |
| 3. Edge cases | concern | Snapshot/source retention and unknown archive path behavior are addressed; changed current-root Markdown evidence is rejected in full-branch selection. |
| 4. Error handling | pass | Selector errors are explicit and fail closed. The error must be corrected at the appropriate narrative-storage boundary, not bypassed as success. |
| 5. Architecture boundaries | concern | Common/specialist/validation ownership is preserved, but stage narrative must use its existing v2 owner. |
| 6. Compatibility | concern | No non-pilot change or historical byte rewrite; current branch CI cannot yet consume the full initiative. |
| 7. Security/privacy | pass | No new execution permissions, publication, customer installation, external effects or secret exposure. Closed unknown-path handling remains intact. |
| 8. Derived artifact currency | pass for M2 scope | No M1 package/canonical input changed. Source hashes/navigation prove archive identities. Final branch/package conclusions still belong to later whole-change review and Verify. |
| 9. Unrelated changes | pass | Exact common-source/consumer scope and necessary selector archive compatibility; no inventory refactor, new schema or service. |
| 10. Validation evidence | concern | M2 scoped reported checks passed, but inspected /tmp/skl-full-branch-ci.log shows selector status blocked on nine sidecars. Passing local checks cannot substitute for the failing integrated branch route. |

## Finding skl-cr-001

- Finding ID: skl-cr-001
- Severity: major
- Location: docs/changes/2026-09-08-skill-model-proposal-family-pilot/*.md (nine newly authored stage narrative notes), scripts/validation_selection.py:1004–1029, and the evidence entries that currently refer readers to those notes.
- Evidence: Full-branch PR CI at 75f13e09 reports unregistered-recording-path for design-authoring.md, design-retained-contract-correction.md, design-contract-transfer-refinement.md, plan-authoring.md, plan-dependency-clarification.md, m1-implementation.md, m1-procedure-walkthrough.md and m2-implementation.md. These are eight named paths in the supplied log despite the parent summary saying nine; the exact emitted list governs. The selector treats each changed path under the current v2 root as a potential supporting record. These files contain stage-owned author/proof narrative, while RF-SR-01 specifies narrative in explicit JSON fields and RF-SR-03 requires its preservation. Existing evidence entries link to this content; deleting it without transfer would lose relied-on proof.
- Required outcome: Preserve complete relied-on narrative and provenance under the existing registered v2 recording contract, and make the actual full branch pass the existing selector route without admitting unknown or retired records. Preserve every prior review judgment, finding origin and exact subject identity; do not rewrite history to hide disappeared sidecars.
- Safe resolution path: Use primary evidence.record operations to embed each complete newly authored note with its original path and raw-byte identity in explicit evidence narrative fields, keeping original procedures/results and exact implementation subjects. Remove only the branch-new sidecars once their complete content is durably represented, so they are absent from the net PR diff. Rereview must compare narrative equivalence and assess removed-subject references explicitly; retained review hashes remain their original observations. Retain unknown Markdown/JSON rejection. Run full-branch selection/CI and applicable record validation after correction. No new registry, schema, broad archive exemption or selector policy redesign is required.
- needs-decision rationale: none for this bounded recording correction under RF-SR-01/03; return to the owning model if a materially different storage/selection contract is proposed.

## Checks, reliance and handoff

Reviewer actually ran git diff/status inspection, targeted/full cat/sed/rg reads, primary subject inspect with full content and the 8388608-byte cap, Python baseline raw-byte equality for all four archive originals, and 73-target archive navigation checks. Inspected author executions: python scripts/test-skill-validator.py (358 passed), guide tests (nine passed), canonical/model/prose checks, focused selector mutation proof, and bash scripts/ci.sh --mode local --timeout 1200 --jobs 4 (scoped pass). Parent's distinct full-branch PR CI produced explicit blocking results before broad execution; it is not reported as passing. Expensive successful suites were not redundantly rerun by this reviewer.

Return the recorded finding to route for bounded correction and independent M2 reassessment. This review does not fix implementation or mutate work state. M2 cannot close yet; fresh final whole-change Code Review and distinct Verify remain mandatory after resolution. No branch, PR, publication or adoption readiness is claimed.
